reason: the design fails 2 of its checks

findings.text: RQLAB-2 is not covered: the only assertion for it is DSCLA-2 And ("the claim label zbuild:claimed contains no hostname component"), but that And is untestable after the When — calling `rsc_render_header` produces rendered markdown; it invokes no label operation and writes no label; a test cannot observe the claim label's name from that call — The label has no hostname in it [FIX IN DESIGN: add or widen a SPEC so it covers this]

DSCLA-2: 1 part to fix
DSCLA-2[code]: When a run starts with an issue, the rendered run-status comment header contains the holder for a local run; the label name has no hostname covers: RQCLA-2, RQLAB-2
  Given: a local run (GITHUB_ACTIONS not true) starts with an issue number
  When: rsc_render_header is called with the run id and holder string
  Then: the rendered header contains <!-- zbuild-holder: run_id=<id> machine=<hostname> -->
  And: the claim label zbuild:claimed contains no hostname component [FIX IN DESIGN: the When is "rsc_render_header is called with the run id and holder string"; `rsc_render_header` (scripts/lib/run-status-render.sh) produces rendered markdown and touches no GitHub label; after this When, no test can observe whether the claim label contains a hostname component — that is a property of `claim_coordinator_claim` in the plugin, not an output of calling the renderer — say what a test can see the code do after the When]

answers: test-author finding 1: done — The original DSCLA-2 combined local and CI sub-cases in a single `Then:` clause ("local runs) or the CI run URL (CI runs)"), which let the test author choose different assertion styles for each sub-case — checking `_ZBUILD_CLAIM_HOLDER` for CI rather than the rendered output. I split DSCLA-2 into two SPECs: DSCLA-2 (local run) and new DSCLA-12 (CI run). Both now say explicitly "When: `rsc_render_header` is called with the run id and holder string" and "Then: the rendered header contains `<!-- zbuild-holder: ... -->`", making it unambiguous that both sub-cases must assert the renderer's output, not the internal holder variable.
